summary: Prince George International Airport (YXS) is the primary air gateway to northern British Columbia, located about 7 km southeast of downtown Prince George, the largest city in the region. Originally established as a wartime airfield during World War II, it has grown into a medium-sized regional hub serving both passenger and cargo traffic. The airport plays a critical role in connecting northern communities and supporting resource industries across central BC.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate from Prince George Airport?
A: Air Canada, WestJet, and Central Mountain Air provide scheduled passenger service, with flights connecting Prince George to Vancouver, Calgary, and several smaller northern destinations. Charter and cargo flights also operate frequently.

Q: Does Prince George Airport have international flights?
A: Despite its international designation, scheduled international passenger routes are limited. The airport is equipped with customs and border services for general aviation and charter international arrivals, primarily supporting cross-border general aviation traffic.

Q: How large is Prince George Airport?
A: It is classified as a medium-sized airport with a main terminal capable of handling moderate passenger volumes. It features a single primary runway suitable for regional jets and smaller cargo aircraft.

Q: Are there car rental services at the airport?
A: Yes, several major car rental agencies operate on-site or provide pickup services at the terminal, making it convenient for travelers exploring northern British Columbia.
transport_tips: Taxis and rideshare services are readily available outside the terminal for the short 10-15 minute trip into downtown Prince George. Shuttle services and rental cars are also options, though renting a vehicle is recommended for those planning to explore the surrounding region. Parking is available on-site for both short-term and long-term stays.
local_tip: If you have a longer layover, head into Prince George to explore the Cottonwood Island Nature Trail or visit the Railway & Forestry Museum—the downtown area is only a quick taxi ride away and offers a taste of true northern BC hospitality.
